brief: review

body: verify.md line 55, Send a test back: 'The run's write stage files a test task for each test sent back' now reads one test task per chunk of each story's sent-back tests; the harm is a stale description a fix verifier reads.

shared.md TEST-CALL-RULE defines departure as a call that departs from an owner answer; test planning now asks the owner nothing, so no planner has an owner answer to depart from, and the kind reads as live when it is not.
converge SKILL.md line 143 lists what the owner list files, and leaves out the product-intent issue it files per program question a sprint's plan records; a reader of the skill misses that route.

ADMINISTRATION.md line 226 still says true-up writes testing.offers ["untested", "stale", "legacy", "runtime"], and its list of the plan's config rewrites does not name the new removal of runtime from testing.offers; the administration document now misstates true-up's former offers

the ## Tests template line '**Runtime:** the runtime scenarios the sprint plans, or none.' predates runtime parts; it should record the runtime parts the sprint plans (the runtime planner's brief line), as SKILL.md section 10 step 2 now says

step 2 files the runtime task with a brief of the inputs line, the questions, and the last run; it could append the groups file's runtime_brief so the brief names the parts; the runtime prompt reads them from the groups file meanwhile

docs/testing.md, section 'A slow product': 'The fix loop files a fixer for the site, keyed perf:, and a verifier, as for a failing test.' Under decision product-slow-fixes-ride-a-round-that-runs-anyway a fixer is filed only beside another failure of the latest whole-suite round, and a lone verdict is deferred to the intake; the standard's ambient copy readers get the old rule.

docs/integration-contract.md:491 lists the vendored agent profiles as ok-haiku, ok-opus, ok-review; the payload now carries ok-drive too, so the contract's list of what true-up vendors is short one profile.

docs/integration-contract.md:491 lists the vendored agent profiles as ok-haiku, ok-opus, and ok-review, without ok-drive and ok-test, and its estate list does not name .ok-planner/lean-profiles.json; a reader of the contract misses two profiles and the record.

brief: story project-spans-folders; drive name project-spans-folders-f72f3ff5

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (testing.enabled off, '- No stack:' facts), I wrote an approved sprint cc-greet with one New story delta and one work item, landed both, and built its certification ledger with the tracker and review verbs as /converge sprint does: review root t1 and three sprint-pass forks closed done, review checks, review drives (driver t5). The driver recorded the sprint's own story as failed (failures item i1, result=failed) and closed t5 done; review merges --source drive filed merge t6, which I left open; no owner-list task ran. I wrote the return block naming the ledger into cc-greet-completion.md and ran .ok-planner/bin/review certified --sprint .ok-planner/sprints/cc-greet.md. The story promises: a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint; the contract's item 3 requires that the run's find loop ran once, and the skill's find loop ends in a merge that folds every failure into the defect list. Saw: exit 0 and 'item 3 (certification): holds: the return block names .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-11-12T000001.jsonl, the review forked pass tasks that closed done, every defect is settled, 0 stuck defects are listed, and the drive ran over 1 of the 1 stories of every story' then 'SPRINT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/sprints/cc-greet.md', and it wrote cc-greet-certified.txt, while the ledger held merge t6 open and the failed drive of the sprint's own story unjudged in the failures pool, never merged into a defect and never filed in the intake. The same verdict came with no merge task filed at all. evidence: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review certification_failures (about line 2048) reads only the defects pool and the review, pass, and drive tasks; it never reads the failures or reports pools, the merge tasks, or the owner-list task.

Reviewed /converge sprint (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md), the sprint boilerplate (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md steps 11 to 13 and the Completion contract), and the script they call, review certified. Diverging line: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review certification_failures, which judges item 3 from the defects pool and the review, pass, and drive tasks alone, so it prints SPRINT COMPLETE and writes the -certified.txt mark while the ledger holds an open merge task and an open failed drive failure on the sprint's own story that no merge sorted and no owner list filed. Story and contract text it diverges from: the story, 'so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; the contract item 3, 'the run's find loop ran once, and every defect stands verified, declined, duplicate, stuck, or promised'; SKILL.md, 'Find. ... a merge agent folds every report into one defect list' and 'Every report and failure the brief names that still stands open goes to the owner list'. A session that skipped or lost the merge gets the same COMPLETE verdict as one that merged, so done depends on the session, not the repository. Divergence: fix.md line 73 tells a fixer 'A fix that must change a behavior a user across a boundary observes, where no ruling allows it, is declined with a question recorded: that change is the owner's to rule on.' But verify.md line 26 (Check each defect) defines the declines a verifier accepts exhaustively: 'A declined defect is not real, the accept list leaves it standing, or its fix lies only in a file the fix line rule above leaves alone' -- the boundary-question decline is not among them, so a verifier following the text sends it back (kickbacks+1) until the defect goes stuck at fix.max_kickbacks, its code restored, and it reaches the owner as a 'Stuck in <run>' issue, or the fixer is pushed to change the boundary behavior without the owner. owner-list.md ('A decline the fixer made with a question recorded ... turns its issue into a judgment issue', under defects 'declined ... with a verified field') and the cheatsheet's Defect issues section ('a verified decline that waits on a boundary question') both presume verifiers accept it. The story promises: defects found and fixed without the owner, so that the owner meets only the questions that need their judgment -- the boundary question should reach the owner as that question, after one decline, not after spent fix rounds as a stuck defect; decision converge-finds-then-fixes: 'A defect whose fixes a verifier rejected up to the limit is no longer mechanical' (stuck is for failed fixes, not for a decline the rules call for). body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 3 (Reconcile), section 9 step 1, section 14 step 4, and {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md, against the sprint document's execution step 2 and decision:closing-commit-baseline. The Reconcile window covers only what stands at Reconcile time: SKILL.md says 'Compute the window. git log --oneline <closed>..HEAD plus the uncommitted tree.' Out-of-band work that appears later in the same session (a path edited during the dialogue, drafting, or code planning) is never sent to the out-of-band reviewer. Code planning step 1 only names such paths ('Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name it to the owner in one line; the planner reads the working tree as it stands'), and the handoff then commits them before the base: '{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}: Where it lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name every such path to the owner, grouped by the work each belongs to, such as ... "out-of-band code" ... ask the owner once whether to commit them'. Those commits land before execution writes its -base.txt, so sprint certification (which judges base..tree) never reviews them, and they land before this sprint's closed: stamp, so the next /plan-sprint's window (closed..HEAD) never contains them either. The same holds for any commit made between approval and the execution base step, which refuses only uncommitted paths ('Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, stop'). No text compares the handoff's paths with what Reconcile reviewed. The story promises: 'an interactive ceremony that turns my goals - and the open design questions and unreconciled work that bear on them - into a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint'. Saw: out-of-band work committed by the handoff, or between approval and the base, falls between two windows and is reconciled by no session, so the corpus can silently disagree with code no ceremony ever reviewed. Fix direction for the owner: rerun the out-of-band review over paths that changed after Reconcile before the handoff commits them, or have the handoff refuse to commit paths Reconcile did not see.

body: Work item 'Runtime parts are planned with no offer' (B8, B9; decision runtime-parts-planned-without-an-offer: 'No standing offer names the runtime parts'). The administration document the /ok session follows still states the old offers. ADMINISTRATION.md 'Declare the lint config' (line 232) says: 'Where testing.enabled, declared or computed, is on, it writes testing.offers ["untested", "stale", "legacy", "runtime"], every kind.' Line 234 says offers holds 'each of untested, stale, legacy, and runtime at most once'. The code now does otherwise: admin/true-up TESTING_OFFERS = ["untested", "stale", "legacy"] (line 2838), former_testing writes three, lint_config_transforms adds the 'testing.offers names runtime ... true-up removes it' rewrite (line 3735), and scripts/plumbline TESTING_OFFERS and scripts/tests OFFERS/offers_listed refuse runtime. The document's list of the config rewrites the plan makes ('the retired compose check names, the retired object form of ports, the retired "checks" key, the citation templates, and ignore') also does not name the new runtime-offer removal. Harm: an /ok session that drafts or amends testing.offers from this text writes runtime, which config-check and the tests tool then refuse, and the document misreports what true-up writes and rewrites (A9). Scope: caused. The sprint edited this file (line 232 gained chunk and group_size in the same sentence) and left the runtime claims, while the same sprint changed the code they describe.

I2 normalizes claimed, recorded, and legacy paths in stray_paths with os.path.normpath. Its premise is that test tasks can record a path as './tests/x.py' while tree_files yields 'tests/x.py'. The sibling in offer_groups (the legacy branch, scripts/tests offer_groups) still compares raw paths: 'claimed = claimed_paths(state["scenarios"])' and then 'if path not in claimed:' against the normalized review.test_paths(root, tree_files(root, folders)). claimed_paths stores scenario test and test_support paths unnormalized. Trigger: the scenario list records a live test as './tests/a_test.py'. Path: tests offers / tests groups -> offer_groups lists tests/a_test.py in a legacy group as a file no scenario claims -> the owner takes that folder -> cmd_groups puts it in the groups file's sort list -> the sort planner is briefed that no scenario claims it -> it can sort the file delete as an orphan -> the legacy task deletes a live test. Harm: A2, a delete reaches a live test, the same harm I2 names. Coding rule 8 asks a fix to cover every member of its class. Scope: the comparison stood the same at the base; the change reaches it, since I2 fixed one member of the class and left this one, and cmd_groups' sort and kept lists depend on it.

body: Work item 'Refile holds its waiters until the refile closes' (outcome: tasks claim never hands out a waiter before the refile closes) is reached only in part. Entry: tasks close <src> --outcome partial|blocked -> cmd_close -> emit(step(run)) -> step issues every drainable task where ready(run, t) -> open_waits counts a dependency as satisfied when d['state'] == CLOSED, whatever its outcome (scripts/tasks:open_waits, 'if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED'). So the close of a partial or blocked task itself issues its waiters and prints them on the run line; both drain forms (skills/_tasks/drain.md, now filling every free slot on each return) start an agent at once, and next_claim/cmd_claim hand the waiter out, since its after list names only closed tasks. The session refiles under sprint-document step 7 only after that return, when the waiter is already running; cmd_refile then touches only waiters with state == OPEN, so it takes nothing back and the waiter builds on the unfinished stage. Evidence in this sprint's own run (.ok-planner/sprints/2026-11-11-eighth-intake-drain-run.jsonl): t5 closed partial 07:17:06, waiter t6 claimed 07:17:17, refile t30 claimed 07:50:00; t11 closed partial 08:04:12, waiter t12 claimed 08:04:23, refile t33 filed after; t28 closed partial 09:18:28, waiter t29 claimed 09:18:35, refile t34 claimed 09:20:46. The I201 readiness check and the refile unissue do not change this path. Scope: the readiness rule stood at base; the change's promised outcome fails through it (reached).

I201 makes next_claim skip, and cmd_claim refuse, an issued task whose after names a task not closed, but step still counts every issued drainable task in waiting_for_agent with no readiness check ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]'), so instructions prints it in the run line's count=. The rule now holds in two places that disagree. Trigger: a run log written before this release, the one the issue fixed, holding an issued, unclaimed waiter of an open refile, resumed under decision:stopped-run-resumes after /ok; step leaves it issued and counted. Path: tasks next -> step -> instructions(count includes the waiter) -> drain fill starts an agent -> tasks claim --agent -> next_claim skips it -> 'no issued task waits for profile ...' -> the agent returns with no closed line -> next lists the same count -> fill starts another agent. While another agent of the profile runs (the refile's), stuck() never fires, so the Workflow drain starts one failing agent per return until the refile closes, spending its lifetime cap; with none running, it returns stuck and the drain's prose names only 'tasks retry <task> on a task left running', which applies to no task. Harm: the run line reports tasks as waiting for an agent that no agent may claim, and the drain acts on it. Scope: caused by the change (I201 added the claim-side check without the count-side one).

body: Artifact: .ok-planner/design/decisions/test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests.md, amended by this sprint and realized by the work item 'Suite faults file no speed step, and product-slow fixes ride a round that runs anyway': 'review certified refuses a sprint ... with a speed send-back that neither settled, returned to its last passing version, nor, as a product-slow verdict a passing whole-suite round left standing, went to the intake'. Code: scripts/tests::settled_failures returns the deferred verdicts apart and never fails on them; cmd_settled prints 'SETTLED: ... and %d product-slow verdicts are deferred to the intake' and exits 0; scripts/review::suite_failures takes exit 0 as item 3 holding. Nothing in tests settled or review certified reads the intake for an issue on each deferred verdict's site. Trigger: the latest whole-suite round passes, a product-slow verdict stands deferred, and the owner list closes without filing its design issue (it skipped it, closed partial, or the run stopped after 2a). Outcome: review certified prints SPRINT COMPLETE though the verdict never reached the intake, so the corpus's stop condition is not checked and the report says done over a verdict that went nowhere. The notes' call ('It does not check that the intake took them, since the owner list files them after it') holds for converge step 2a, which runs before the owner list, but not for review certified, which runs after the close. Scope: caused; the sprint added the deferral and the decision sentence.

Entry A3 (a stall on a correctly configured project). Trigger: the first sprint that plans tests on a project whose scenario list records no test yet. stage_preflight (scripts/tests) files the preflight wherever the plan's budget carries no preflight mark equal to the state's budget, so that first sprint gets one, while its planned tests are not written. Path: tests tasks --stage write -> scripts/tests::stage_preflight -> test-preflight.md checks 6 and 7. Check 6 says 'run one recorded test that needs the stack, or any recorded test where none needs it: .ok-planner/bin/tests run --only <the test>. Check that each setup run exits 0 and the test passes'; check 7 reads readiness from 'the recorded test of check 6 ... when it passes again'. Check 5 has a skip branch ('Where no two recorded tests share a slug, skip this check'); 6 and 7 have none, and tests run --only refuses a scenario with no live test ('no live test for ...'). The prompt then says 'Where a check of the suite run, 5 to 7, fails, close blocked', the write stage refiles the preflight once, and 'a preflight that closes blocked twice is a genuine blocker' (stage_preflight raises), so the sprint's test stages stop on a check nothing can pass. The same gap stands in skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md section 3.7 checks 2 and 3 when /ok-setup turns testing on before any test is recorded: the check cannot pass, and the owner is asked to change a command or setup that is not at fault. Scope: caused; the sprint added checks 5 to 7 and 3.7's three checks.

Entry A9, with coding rule 3.6 (elapsed time from one clock). The line-timing check in test-preflight.md check 5 and ok-setup section 3.7 check 1 passes only where 'the later test's arrived less its seconds is at or after the earlier test's arrived', and applies that test even where both lines carry started and ended. arrived is the tests tool's monotonic clock (scripts/tests::take_line, time.monotonic() - started); seconds is measured by the suite command. The check subtracts a duration on one clock from a time on the other with no allowance, the comparison docs/testing.md and decision tests-isolated-unless-declared reject for the schedule check because 'overlaps of a few milliseconds failed two rounds in which every test passed'. Trigger: a runner that writes each line as its test ends through a reporter a few milliseconds behind the worker (a controller process, as pytest-xdist uses), or whose seconds include setup that began before the earlier line reached the stream. Outcome: the later test's arrived less seconds lands a few milliseconds before the earlier test's arrived; the preflight closes blocked naming a runner fault that does not exist, is refiled once, then stage_preflight raises a genuine blocker; in /ok-setup the owner is asked to change a command that writes its lines correctly. Scope: caused; the sprint added the check.

body: Work item 'The write stage refiles a blocked test task that waits on another blocked test task' (B24), also reached through 'A test task takes a story's scenarios, up to testing.chunk'. Entry: tests tasks --stage write -> cmd_tasks -> stage_write -> pending loop -> planned_refile -> mapped_waits -> loop_refusals. Trigger: two test tasks that share a test file both close blocked having filed test-support items, where the task that waits on the other (through holders when it was filed) has the key that sorts first as a string. Example: with testing.chunk 1, the value true-up writes, a story with 10 or more scenarios in one test file files test:S:1..test:S:12, each waiting on the one before through the shared file; when they all close blocked on one missing helper, blocked_on_test_support returns them sorted by key string (test:S:1, test:S:10, test:S:11, test:S:12, test:S:2, ...). body: B213/B218 (I201), stored-state boundary: a run log an earlier release wrote, resumed by a new /goal or drained across an update. No ruling names that user: B213 says only 'the run log keeps its record shape'. Before the change, a waiter that was issued before its dependency was refiled stayed issued (the refile-leaves-waiters-issued bug). Such a run log holds an open, issued task whose after names an open refile. The resume's 'tasks retry --all' unissues it only where the refile itself is reopened (running or closed retryable), so a refile that stood open and unclaimed at the stop leaves the waiter issued. After the change, step (scripts/tasks:step, 'waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]') still counts that task in the run line's count=, but next_claim now skips it ('... and ready(run, t)') and cmd_claim refuses it ('task %s still waits on %s'). So the count tells the drain a task is claimable that no claim can take. The drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md fill/stuck) starts an agent for it. That agent's 'claim --agent' fails with 'no issued task waits for profile X; run tasks next first', and next lists the same count. If an agent of the same profile holds the refile, the drain refills on every return and burns an agent each time until the refile closes. Otherwise it returns 'stuck' and names 'tasks retry <task> on a task left running' as the only move, which does not apply to an open issued task. Before: the waiter was claimed early, which is the bug. After: the count disagrees with claim (A9 harm: a count that does not match what an agent can take). Scope: caused by the change, which made claim stricter than the issued mark that step counts; reached only through a run log written by the base release.

body: B212. Decision ancestor-claude-md-left-to-the-owner commits that the administration 'names each such file that the project's harness settings do not already exclude'. ancestor_memory_lines decides exclusion with fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) (admin/true-up: 'if os.path.isfile(path) and not any(p == path or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) for p in patterns)'). fnmatch's '*' and '?' match '/', so a claudeMdExcludes glob that the harness matches path-segment-wise (glob syntax, where '*' stops at '/') counts as excluding deeper files the harness still loads. Trigger: settings.json claudeMdExcludes ['/Users/*/CLAUDE.md'] and a project at /Users/me/work/proj with /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md: fnmatch says excluded, so diagnose prints no recommend: line for /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md, while the harness loads it into every session and agent. Harm: the one report the decision promises is silently skipped for a file the settings do not exclude. Note the harness's glob semantics come from the harness, not this tree; the merge agent should weigh that. Scope: caused by the change (ancestor_memory_lines is new in this sprint).

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 3 (Reconcile), section 9 step 1, section 14 step 4, and {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md, against the sprint document's execution step 2 and decision:closing-commit-baseline. The Reconcile window covers only what stands at Reconcile time: SKILL.md says 'Compute the window. git log --oneline <closed>..HEAD plus the uncommitted tree.' Out-of-band work that appears later in the same session (a path edited during the dialogue, drafting, or code planning) is never sent to the out-of-band reviewer. Code planning step 1 only names such paths ('Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name it to the owner in one line; the planner reads the working tree as it stands'), and the handoff then commits them before the base: '{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}: Where it lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name every such path to the owner, grouped by the work each belongs to, such as ... "out-of-band code" ... ask the owner once whether to commit them'. Those commits land before execution writes its -base.txt, so sprint certification (which judges base..tree) never reviews them, and they land before this sprint's closed: stamp, so the next /plan-sprint's window (closed..HEAD) never contains them either. The same holds for any commit made between approval and the execution base step, which refuses only uncommitted paths ('Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, stop'). No text compares the handoff's paths with what Reconcile reviewed. The story promises: 'an interactive ceremony that turns my goals - and the open design questions and unreconciled work that bear on them - into a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint'. Saw: out-of-band work committed by the handoff, or between approval and the base, falls between two windows and is reconciled by no session, so the corpus can silently disagree with code no ceremony ever reviewed. Fix direction for the owner: rerun the out-of-band review over paths that changed after Reconcile before the handoff commits them, or have the handoff refuse to commit paths Reconcile did not see.

Step 4, in a sprint that opens test stages, tells the session to drain inside step 4 itself, before the step that creates the checklist: line 287, 'Drain with step 7's loop. After each drain, run tests tasks --sprint <this sprint's path> --stage verify ...'. The test write stage is filed --after the code stages' build tasks, so that drain runs every build stage. The checklist step comes later in reading order, step 6 at line 327-329: 'Keep the progress checklist. ... Create one entry per stage when the build tasks are filed.' A session working the numbered steps in order, under testing on (as this project runs), lands every code stage in step 4's drain before it reaches step 6, so the owner's session shows no checklist while the stages land. The story promises: 'a way to see from my session which stages of a running sprint have landed, each time the run reports back to my session'. Decision task-tools-mirror-the-report: 'The checklist is its own numbered step, with its three moments named, because an executor skips a checklist written as a trailing clause after the report-rendering step: a measured execution under that form ran its first three agents with no checklist'. Step 6 names its moment by event, but step 4's embedded drain puts the first drain ahead of it in the order the executor reads, the same failure the decision names. The rest holds: true-up diagnose prints 'WIRING NEEDED (ok-planner, env)' with the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS entry, wire-env writes it and repairs a value of 0, and the Workflow return's step 3 reads keys from tasks report's key column, which the tracker prints.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:How to execute steps 4 and 6; A3; step 4 (sprint-document.md:287) says 'Drain with step 7's loop' for the test stages, which wait on every code stage's build task, before step 6 (:327-329) says 'Keep the progress checklist ... Create one entry per stage when the build tasks are filed', so an executor working the steps in order lands every code stage before it reaches the checklist, against story watch-execution-progress and the rationale of decision task-tools-mirror-the-report (an executor skips a checklist that comes after the work in reading order). Outside the sprint: the same order stood at base 46aeb75 (base step 4 'Drain with step 7's loop' at :237, step 6 'Keep the progress checklist' at :273, its text unchanged); the sprint's step-4 edits changed which tasks the write stage files, not the drain's place before the checklist.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_verify. What it does: B22 (rewrite) groups every tests item awaiting its verifier by its recording task and keys the verify task 'verify:%s' % recorder, skipping a key already in existing (scripts/tests:4736-4743: 'awaiting.setdefault(item.get("task") or item["id"], []).append(item)', 'if ("verify", key) in existing: continue'); at the base the key was verify:<tests item id>. User left behind: the stopped-run resume path (decision stopped-run-resumes; sprint-document step 3 'tasks retry --all', which reopens a blocked or partial task under its own id, and step 4's '--stage verify after each drain'). Trigger: test task T closes blocked or partial having recorded scenario A's tests item; the verify stage files verify:T for A; the run stops before T is refiled; the resume reopens T under the same id; T records B. Before: B's item got verify:<B's item id>. Now: B groups under T, verify:T is in existing, and no verify task is ever filed for B; awaits_verifier(B) stays true, so --stage speed --from state refuses on it and the run cannot proceed (R3: a rewrite left a user in the release behind). Scope: caused by B22. Report: i28.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:step. What it does: step counts every open issued task ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]', scripts/tasks:867) into the run line's count, while next_claim takes only a task that is also ready ('... and ready(run, t)', 1121) and cmd_claim refuses one that still waits ('task %s still waits on %s; claim it once each of them closes', 1149). Boundary user no ruling names (R5, B213/B218, stored state): a run log the base release wrote, resumed by a new /goal or drained across an update. At the base a waiter issued before its dependency was refiled stayed issued, so such a log holds an open, issued task whose after names an open refile; tasks retry --all unissues it only where it reissues that refile, so a refile that stood open and unclaimed at the stop leaves the waiter issued. B213 says only 'the run log keeps its record shape'. Harm: next reports a count of claimable tasks no claim can take; the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md) starts an agent whose 'claim --agent' fails, refills on every return while another agent holds the refile, or returns stuck naming 'tasks retry' on a task left running, which does not apply. Scope: caused; the change made claim stricter than the issued mark step counts. Report: i30.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:undriven_failure, reached from certification_failures. What it does: certification_failures computes 'reason = undriven_reason(root, tasks) if undriven and not driven else None' (scripts/review, certification_failures); undriven_reason ends 'return "no driver task was filed"' where drive-stack prints none, or stack with no failed stack-start exec task; undriven_failure then writes 'its latest driver task %s %s' and appends '; the drive did not run: %s' % reason whenever reason differs. Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> where the ledger holds driver tasks for the required stories and none closed done with a result (each closed partial, or was never claimed), on this project (drive-stack none). Harm (A9): each item 3 line reads '<ledger> drove no story <slug>: its latest driver task tN closed partial; the drive did not run: no driver task was filed; ...', telling the operator acting on SPRINT NOT COMPLETE, and the stop record built from it, that no driver was filed in the line that names one. Scope: caused; B118 narrowed driven_stories to drivers that closed done, and the new undriven_failure appends the fallback beside a filed driver; at the base the fallback ran only where no driver task existed. Report: i31.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:How to execute steps 5, 10, and 13, against step 3a. What it does: steps 5 and 13 add '--planning .ok-planner/sprints/<sprint-name>-test-planning.jsonl where step 3a ran' to tasks render (sprint-document.md:322-325, 446-449), and step 10 shows the plan: calls 'Where step 3a ran' (388); step 3a says 'A sprint whose plan already stands beside it keeps that plan and skips this step' (227-228). Trigger: a run that stopped after step 3a assembled the plan and is resumed by the same goal line, as step 11 and decision stopped-run-resumes say it is: in the resumed session step 3a is skipped. Harm (A9): read as written, step 13's render omits --planning and the completion report's ## Calls drops every plan: row, so the calls table the owner reads to veto each judgment an agent made without the owner reports fewer calls than the run made. The migrated boilerplate lines in admin/retired-boilerplate.json follow the template. Scope: caused; step 3a and the --planning render are new in this sprint. Report: i37.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:ancestor_memory_lines. What it does: it decides whether claudeMdExcludes excludes an ancestor CLAUDE.md with 'not any(p == path or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) for p in patterns)' (true-up:959); fnmatch's * and ? match /, where the harness matches claudeMdExcludes as globs whose * stops at a path separator. Trigger: claudeMdExcludes ['/Users/*/CLAUDE.md'] and a project at /Users/me/work/proj with /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md: fnmatch counts the file excluded, diagnose prints no recommend line for it, and the harness still loads it into every session and agent. Harm (A8, a commitment of decision ancestor-claude-md-left-to-the-owner: 'The front door's administration names each such file that the project's harness settings do not already exclude'): the named report is skipped for a file the settings do not exclude. Scope: caused; ancestor_memory_lines is new in this sprint. Report: i38.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:How to execute step 2. What it does: B208's check stands as its own unconditioned sentence after the test-stage condition: '...the run opens its test stages (step 3), and .ok-planner/bin/tests is required too: where it is missing, stop and say so. Then run .ok-planner/bin/tests profiles and show its output whole. Where it refuses, ... stop' (sprint-document.md:134-146), where the notes scope it 'Step 2: where the run opens test stages, run .ok-planner/bin/tests profiles'. User: the executing session of a sprint that opens no test stages (testing.enabled off, or no groups file that plans tests and no -plan.json), an approved sprint migrated through admin/retired-boilerplate.json or a new one; step 3 registers ok-test only where step 2 found the run opens test stages. Trigger: .ok-planner/lean-profiles.json missing, or a .claude/rules/ cheatsheet differing from its recorded SHA-256. Before (base): the run starts and builds. Now: it writes a stop record and stops at step 2, though no task will run on ok-test (R4, a change the notes do not list breaks a user in the release). Same flaw as i43 in area sprint-2. Scope: caused; the sentence is new in this sprint. Report: i32.

Entry A3 (a stall on a correctly configured project). Trigger: the first sprint that plans tests on a project whose scenario list records no test yet. stage_preflight (scripts/tests) files the preflight wherever the plan's budget carries no preflight mark equal to the state's budget, so that first sprint gets one, while its planned tests are not written. Path: tests tasks --stage write -> scripts/tests::stage_preflight -> test-preflight.md checks 6 and 7. Check 6 says 'run one recorded test that needs the stack, or any recorded test where none needs it: .ok-planner/bin/tests run --only <the test>. Check that each setup run exits 0 and the test passes'; check 7 reads readiness from 'the recorded test of check 6 ... when it passes again'. Check 5 has a skip branch ('Where no two recorded tests share a slug, skip this check'); 6 and 7 have none, and tests run --only refuses a scenario with no live test ('no live test for ...'). The prompt then says 'Where a check of the suite run, 5 to 7, fails, close blocked', the write stage refiles the preflight once, and 'a preflight that closes blocked twice is a genuine blocker' (stage_preflight raises), so the sprint's test stages stop on a check nothing can pass. The same gap stands in skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md section 3.7 checks 2 and 3 when /ok-setup turns testing on before any test is recorded: the check cannot pass, and the owner is asked to change a command or setup that is not at fault. Scope: caused; the sprint added checks 5 to 7 and 3.7's three checks.

Entry A9, with coding rule 3.6 (elapsed time from one clock). The line-timing check in test-preflight.md check 5 and ok-setup section 3.7 check 1 passes only where 'the later test's arrived less its seconds is at or after the earlier test's arrived', and applies that test even where both lines carry started and ended. arrived is the tests tool's monotonic clock (scripts/tests::take_line, time.monotonic() - started); seconds is measured by the suite command. The check subtracts a duration on one clock from a time on the other with no allowance, the comparison docs/testing.md and decision tests-isolated-unless-declared reject for the schedule check because 'overlaps of a few milliseconds failed two rounds in which every test passed'. Trigger: a runner that writes each line as its test ends through a reporter a few milliseconds behind the worker (a controller process, as pytest-xdist uses), or whose seconds include setup that began before the earlier line reached the stream. Outcome: the later test's arrived less seconds lands a few milliseconds before the earlier test's arrived; the preflight closes blocked naming a runner fault that does not exist, is refiled once, then stage_preflight raises a genuine blocker; in /ok-setup the owner is asked to change a command that writes its lines correctly. Scope: caused; the sprint added the check.

Work item 'The write stage refiles a blocked test task that waits on another blocked test task' (B24), also reached through 'A test task takes a story's scenarios, up to testing.chunk'. Entry: tests tasks --stage write -> cmd_tasks -> stage_write -> pending loop -> planned_refile -> mapped_waits -> loop_refusals. Trigger: two test tasks that share a test file both close blocked having filed test-support items, where the task that waits on the other (through holders when it was filed) has the key that sorts first as a string. Example: with testing.chunk 1, the value true-up writes, a story with 10 or more scenarios in one test file files test:S:1..test:S:12, each waiting on the one before through the shared file; when they all close blocked on one missing helper, blocked_on_test_support returns them sorted by key string (test:S:1, test:S:10, test:S:11, test:S:12, test:S:2, ...). The pending loop plans test:S:10's refile first; holders[F] is +a, so test:S:2's refile, planned later, gets +a in its waits (waits |= holders[path] for task.files, scripts/tests stage_write: 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}'), while mapped_waits maps test:S:10's copied wait on test:S:9 to test:S:9's planned refile ('filing["after"] = sorted({planned.get(dep, dep) for dep in latest})'), which chains back to test:S:2. The refiles wait on each other, loop_refusals refuses ('would wait on itself through ...'), and the write stage files nothing, which sprint-document step 7 makes a genuine blocker that stops the run. The same holds across stories: story zeta's task filed first holds a shared test file, story alpha's task waits on it, and test:alpha:1 sorts first. Outcome not reached: the stage refuses instead of refiling a blocked test task that waits on another blocked test task. Scope: caused. At the base the mapping dropped a wait on a refile planned later (planned[dep][0] < n), so no cycle formed; this sprint maps every copied wait through every planned refile and numbers chunk keys, which together close the loop.

Work item 'A lean test profile runs the test stages' test-support, test, verify, and speed tasks' says the start checks in the execution section "run the same check wherever the run opens test stages" (decision stale-lean-body-stops-test-work: "no sprint run that opens test stages starts"). Step 2 of plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md closes the test-stage condition at "where it is missing, stop and say so." and then states the check as its own unconditioned sentence: "Then run `.ok-planner/bin/tests profiles` and show its output whole. Where it refuses, ... stop, the stop record naming each file it names". An executor reading the boilerplate runs the check on every sprint, so a sprint that opens no test stages (testing.enabled off, no groups file, no plan) stops with a stop record whenever a cheatsheet under .claude/rules/ differs from .ok-planner/lean-profiles.json or the record is missing. The outcome reaches the check only in part: it is not bound to the runs that open test stages, and it stops runs the work item and the decision let start. Scope: caused (the sentence is new in this sprint; the base step 2 ended at the tests-missing check). The replaced boilerplate lines in admin/retired-boilerplate.json follow the template.

B22 (rewrite): stage_verify now keys each verify task verify:<the recording test task's id> and skips a key already in existing (tests:4740-4743), where the base keyed verify:<tests item id>. User in the release left behind: the stopped-run resume path (decision stopped-run-resumes; sprint-document step 4 'run --stage verify after each drain', and the reopen branch blocked_on_test_support/reopened_on_test_support, tests:4399-4413, annotated @decision: stopped-run-resumes). A resumed run reopens a blocked or partial task under its own id with 'tasks retry --all' (project.md: retry 'reopens a task that closed blocked, partial, disputed, or failed'). Trigger: chunk test task T7 (scenarios A, B) closes blocked or partial having recorded A's tests item; the verify stage files verify:T7 for A; the run stops before T7 is refiled; the resume reopens T7 with the same id; T7 runs again and records B (and possibly A again). Old outcome: B's item got verify:<B's item id>, a fresh verifier. New outcome: awaits_verifier(B) groups under recorder T7, key verify:T7 is already in existing, so no verify task is filed for B ever; --stage speed --from state then refuses on B awaiting its verifier (speed_refusal), and the write/verify loop files nothing, so the run cannot proceed. Scope: caused by the change (B22).

B213/B218 (I201), stored-state boundary: a run log an earlier release wrote, resumed by a new /goal or drained across an update. No ruling names that user: B213 says only 'the run log keeps its record shape'. Before the change, a waiter that was issued before its dependency was refiled stayed issued (the refile-leaves-waiters-issued bug). Such a run log holds an open, issued task whose after names an open refile. The resume's 'tasks retry --all' unissues it only where the refile itself is reopened (running or closed retryable), so a refile that stood open and unclaimed at the stop leaves the waiter issued. After the change, step (scripts/tasks:step, 'waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]') still counts that task in the run line's count=, but next_claim now skips it ('... and ready(run, t)') and cmd_claim refuses it ('task %s still waits on %s'). So the count tells the drain a task is claimable that no claim can take. The drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md fill/stuck) starts an agent for it. That agent's 'claim --agent' fails with 'no issued task waits for profile X; run tasks next first', and next lists the same count. If an agent of the same profile holds the refile, the drain refills on every return and burns an agent each time until the refile closes. Otherwise it returns 'stuck' and names 'tasks retry <task> on a task left running' as the only move, which does not apply to an open issued task. Before: the waiter was claimed early, which is the bug. After: the count disagrees with claim (A9 harm: a count that does not match what an agent can take). Scope: caused by the change, which made claim stricter than the issued mark that step counts; reached only through a run log written by the base release.

A9 (C2 on B102/B118). Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> where the certification ledger holds driver tasks for the required stories (brief 'story <slug>; ...') and none of them closed done with a non-empty result (e.g. each closed partial, or was never claimed), and review drive-stack prints 'none' (this project) or 'stack' with no failed stack-start exec task. Path: scripts/review:cmd_certified -> certification_failures: 'reason = undriven_reason(root, tasks) if undriven and not driven else None' -> undriven_reason falls through to its last line 'return "no driver task was filed"' -> undriven_failure: 'why = "its latest driver task %s %s" % (drivers[-1]["id"], driver_standing(drivers[-1]))' then 'if reason and reason != why: why += "; the drive did not run: %s" % reason'. Harm: each item 3 failure line reads '<ledger> drove no story <slug>: its latest driver task tN closed partial; the drive did not run: no driver task was filed; the drive takes ...' — it says no driver task was filed in the same line that names the filed driver task; the operator acting on SPRINT NOT COMPLETE (and the stop record built from these lines) is told the drivers were never filed. At the base, undriven_reason ran only when no 'story ' driver task existed at all (driven_stories counted every filed driver), so its fallback was true there. Scope: caused by the change (B118 narrowed driven_stories to drivers that closed done, and the new undriven_failure appends undriven_reason's fallback beside a filed driver).

Steps 5 and 13 add --planning .ok-planner/sprints/<sprint-name>-test-planning.jsonl to tasks render only 'where step 3a ran', and step 10 shows the plan: calls 'Where step 3a ran'. Step 3a itself says 'A sprint whose plan already stands beside it keeps that plan and skips this step.' Trigger: a run that stopped after step 3a assembled the plan (any genuine blocker, a SPRINT NOT COMPLETE, or a session ending) and is resumed by the same goal line, as step 11 and the goal rule say it is. In the resumed session the plan stands, so step 3a is skipped and did not run in this session; read as written, step 13's render after certification omits --planning, and the completion report's ## Calls drops every plan: row: each call the test planners made (rewrites to a changed outcome, retires as a gap, outcomes left untested). Harm: the calls table the owner reads to veto every judgment an agent made without the owner reports fewer calls than the run made, so the owner never sees, and cannot veto, the test planning calls. The condition that would hold on every path is whether the planning run file stands beside the sprint, not whether 3a ran in this session. Scope: caused by this sprint's change (step 3a and the --planning render are new).

B212. Decision ancestor-claude-md-left-to-the-owner commits that the administration 'names each such file that the project's harness settings do not already exclude'. ancestor_memory_lines decides exclusion with fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) (admin/true-up: 'if os.path.isfile(path) and not any(p == path or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) for p in patterns)'). fnmatch's '*' and '?' match '/', so a claudeMdExcludes glob that the harness matches path-segment-wise (glob syntax, where '*' stops at '/') counts as excluding deeper files the harness still loads. Trigger: settings.json claudeMdExcludes ['/Users/*/CLAUDE.md'] and a project at /Users/me/work/proj with /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md: fnmatch says excluded, so diagnose prints no recommend: line for /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md, while the harness loads it into every session and agent. Harm: the one report the decision promises is silently skipped for a file the settings do not exclude. Note the harness's glob semantics come from the harness, not this tree; the merge agent should weigh that. Scope: caused by the change (ancestor_memory_lines is new in this sprint).

B208 widened past its notes. The notes for the lean test profile (Changes, sprint-document.md) scope the new check: 'Step 2: where the run opens test stages, run .ok-planner/bin/tests profiles. If it refuses, stop as step 11 says.' The carried step 2 puts it after the test-stage conditional as a separate sentence: '...the run opens its test stages (step 3), and .ok-planner/bin/tests is required too: where it is missing, stop and say so. Then run .ok-planner/bin/tests profiles and show its output whole. Where it refuses, ... stop'. Read as written, every run executes it, including a sprint under testing.enabled off, or one with no groups file that plans tests and no -plan.json, which opens no test stages and never registers or files ok-test (step 3 registers ok-test only where step 2 found the run opens test stages; converge step 3 likewise registers it only where the testing state is not off). User: the executing session of such a sprint (an approved sprint across the trued-up boundary, migrated through retired-boilerplate.json, or a new one). Goal (notes, B208 Changes): the lean-record check gates only runs that file test-stage tasks. Trigger: .ok-planner/lean-profiles.json missing or a .claude/rules/ cheatsheet differing from its recorded SHA-256. Old outcome (base): the run starts and builds. New outcome: the run writes a stop record and stops at step 2, though no test task will ever run on ok-test. Scope: caused by this sprint's change (the sentence is new in this sprint).

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:Declare the lint config. The administration document the /ok session follows still says true-up writes runtime as a standing offer, contradicting decision runtime-parts-planned-without-an-offer ('No standing offer names the runtime parts'), which this sprint added and whose work item 'Runtime parts are planned with no offer' changed admin/true-up (TESTING_OFFERS = ["untested", "stale", "legacy"], line 2838; the 'testing.offers names runtime ... true-up removes it' transform, line 3735), scripts/plumbline, and scripts/tests to refuse runtime. Evidence: ADMINISTRATION.md:232 'it writes testing.offers ["untested", "stale", "legacy", "runtime"], every kind'; ADMINISTRATION.md:234 'offers, the kinds of work /plan-sprint offers, each of untested, stale, legacy, and runtime at most once'; the list of the plan's config rewrites at line 232 ('the retired compose check names, the retired object form of ports, the retired "checks" key, the citation templates, and ignore') leaves out the new runtime-offer removal. Trigger: an /ok session drafts or amends testing.offers from this text. Harm: it writes runtime, which config-check and the tests tool refuse, and the document misreports what true-up writes and rewrites. Scope: caused; the sprint edited line 232 and left these claims. Reports: i17 (sprint-1), i4 (sprint-noticed).

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:## Tests template. Work item 'Detailed test planning runs in sprint execution, ahead of the build' says the template records 'the runtime parts the sprint plans'. The template line, new in this sprint, reads (sprint-document.md:70) '- **Runtime:** the runtime scenarios the sprint plans, or none.' SKILL.md:220 says to write 'the runtime parts the sprint plans, from the runtime planner's brief line', and SKILL.md:242 has Approval present 'the runtime parts the sprint plans'. Trigger: a /plan-sprint session writes the ## Tests section from the template. At that time no runtime scenario is planned, since execution plans them in step 3a. Outcome not reached: the session writes 'none' or invents scenarios, and the scope the owner approves misstates which runtime parts get tests. Scope: caused; the sprint wrote the template. Reports: i19 (sprint-1), i5 (sprint-noticed).

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:offer_groups (legacy branch), with claimed_paths. Improvement I2 normalized claimed, recorded, and legacy paths in stray_paths with os.path.normpath, because test tasks can record './tests/x.py' while tree_files yields 'tests/x.py' (harm A2: a live test reads as stray and is deleted). The sibling comparison in offer_groups still compares raw paths: 'claimed = claimed_paths(state["scenarios"])' then 'if path not in claimed:' against review.test_paths(root, tree_files(root, folders)), and claimed_paths adds scenario['test']['path'] and test_support_of(scenario) unnormalized. Rule: plumbline-coding rule 8 (a defect is one instance of a class; fix every member in the same change), which decides the fix. Trigger: the scenario list records a live test as './tests/a_test.py'. Path: tests offers / tests groups -> offer_groups lists tests/a_test.py in a legacy group as a file no scenario claims -> the owner takes the folder -> cmd_groups puts it in the sort list -> the sort planner may sort it delete -> the legacy task deletes a live test (A2). Scope: the sprint fixed one member of the class (I2) and changed both offer_groups (runtime group removed) and claimed_paths (test_support_of), leaving this member. Report: i18.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:open_waits (read by ready, step, next_claim, cmd_claim). Work item 'Refile holds its waiters until the refile closes' promises 'tasks claim never hands out a waiter before the refile closes'. open_waits counts a dependency satisfied when it is CLOSED whatever its outcome ('if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED'). Entry: tasks close <src> --outcome partial|blocked -> cmd_close -> step issues every drainable task where ready(run, t) -> the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md, filling every free slot) starts an agent -> next_claim/cmd_claim hand out the waiter. The session refiles only after that return (sprint-document step 7), when the waiter already runs; cmd_refile touches only waiters with state == OPEN, so it takes nothing back and the waiter builds on the unfinished stage. User left behind: the stopped-run resume path (decision stopped-run-resumes; sprint-document step 3 'tasks retry --all', which reopens a blocked or partial task under its own id, and step 4's '--stage verify after each drain'). Trigger: test task T closes blocked or partial having recorded scenario A's tests item; the verify stage files verify:T for A; the run stops before T is refiled; the resume reopens T under the same id; T records B. Before: B's item got verify:<B's item id>. Now: B groups under T, verify:T is in existing, and no verify task is ever filed for B; awaits_verifier(B) stays true, so --stage speed --from state refuses on it and the run cannot proceed (R3: a rewrite left a user in the release behind). Scope: caused by B22. Report: i28.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i46 i62 i63
- i46: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:step. What it does: step counts every open issued task ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]', scripts/tasks:867) into the run line's count, while next_claim takes only a task that is also ready ('... and ready(run, t)', 1121) and cmd_claim refuses one that still waits ('task %s still waits on %s; claim it once each of them closes', 1149). Boundary user no ruling names (R5, B213/B218, stored state): a run log the base release wrote, resumed by a new /goal or drained across an update. At the base a waiter issued before its dependency was refiled stayed issued, so such a log holds an open, issued task whose after names an open refile; tasks retry --all unissues it only where it reissues that refile, so a refile that stood open and unclaimed at the stop leaves the waiter issued. B213 says only 'the run log keeps its record shape'. Harm: next reports a count of claimable tasks no claim can take; the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md) starts an agent whose 'claim --agent' fails, refills on every return while another agent holds the refile, or returns stuck naming 'tasks retry' on a task left running, which does not apply. Scope: caused; the change made claim stricter than the issued mark step counts. Report: i30.
- i62: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:open_waits (read by ready, step, next_claim, cmd_claim). Work item 'Refile holds its waiters until the refile closes' promises 'tasks claim never hands out a waiter before the refile closes'. open_waits counts a dependency satisfied when it is CLOSED whatever its outcome ('if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED'). Entry: tasks close <src> --outcome partial|blocked -> cmd_close -> step issues every drainable task where ready(run, t) -> the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md, filling every free slot) starts an agent -> next_claim/cmd_claim hand out the waiter. The session refiles only after that return (sprint-document step 7), when the waiter already runs; cmd_refile touches only waiters with state == OPEN, so it takes nothing back and the waiter builds on the unfinished stage. Evidence from this sprint's run (.ok-planner/sprints/2026-11-11-eighth-intake-drain-run.jsonl): t5 closed partial 07:17:06, waiter t6 claimed 07:17:17, refile t30 claimed 07:50:00; t11 closed partial 08:04:12, waiter t12 claimed 08:04:23; t28 closed partial 09:18:28, waiter t29 claimed 09:18:35, refile t34 claimed 09:20:46. Outcome reached only in part. Scope: the readiness rule stood at base; the work item's promised outcome fails through it. Report: i20.
- i63: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:step. I201 makes next_claim skip, and cmd_claim refuse, an issued task whose after names a task not closed, but step counts every issued drainable task with no readiness check ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]'), so instructions prints it in the run line's count=. Trigger: a run log written by the base release holding an issued, unclaimed waiter of an open refile, resumed under decision stopped-run-resumes after /ok. Path: tasks next -> step -> instructions (count includes the waiter) -> the drain starts an agent -> tasks claim --agent -> next_claim skips it -> 'no issued task waits for profile ...' -> next prints the same count -> the drain starts another agent while the refile's agent runs, or returns stuck naming only 'tasks retry <task> on a task left running'. Harm (A9): the run line reports tasks waiting for an agent that no agent may claim, and the drain acts on it. Scope: caused; I201 added the claim-side check without the count-side one. Same flaw as i46 (sprint-10). Report: i21.

Now: B groups under T, verify:T is in existing, and no verify task is ever filed for B; awaits_verifier(B) stays true, so --stage speed --from state refuses on it and the run cannot proceed (R3: a rewrite left a user in the release behind). body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md:Check 6 and 7. What it does: checks 6 and 7 tell the preflight to 'run one recorded test that needs the stack, or any recorded test where none needs it: .ok-planner/bin/tests run --only <the test>. Check that each setup run exits 0 and the test passes' (test-preflight.md:47-52), and check 7 reads readiness from 'the recorded test of check 6 ... when it passes again' (53-59); unlike check 5 ('Where no two recorded tests share a slug, skip this check', 45-46), neither has a branch for a scenario list that records no test. Trigger: the first sprint that plans tests on a project whose scenario list records no test and whose plan names a stack; scripts/tests::stage_preflight (4487-4502) files the preflight wherever the budget carries no preflight mark equal to the state's budget. Harm (A3, on the change): checks 6 and 7 cannot pass, the prompt says 'Where a check of the suite run, 5 to 7, fails, close blocked' (64-66), the write stage refiles once, and stage_preflight raises 'closed blocked twice ... surface it as a genuine blocker' (4503-4505), so the sprint's test stages stop on a check nothing can pass. The report's ok-setup half does not hold: skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md 3.7 line 127 says 'Where the scenario list records no test, say so in one line, and end the step', before its three checks. Scope: caused; checks 5 to 7 are new in this sprint. Report: i24.
note: test-preflight.md checks 6 and 7 now carry a branch for a scenario list that records no test: check 6 checks only that each setup run exits 0, and check 7 only that setup exits 0 and the scratch resource still stands, so no check needs a recorded test that cannot exist and the preflight no longer closes blocked twice on it. ok-setup SKILL.md 3.7 already ends the step where no test is recorded; unchanged for this defect. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md:Check 5, and the same check in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md 3.7 check 1 (line 135). What it does: the line-timing check passes only where 'the later test's arrived less its seconds is at or after the earlier test's arrived, and, where both lines carry started and ended, the later test's started is at or after the earlier test's ended' (test-preflight.md:42-45): it applies the arrival test always, even where both lines carry the command's clock. arrived is the tests tool's monotonic clock (scripts/tests::take_line:2762, 'arrived = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)'); seconds is the suite command's. The schedule check takes the arrival span only where a pair is not clocked on the command's clock (scripts/tests::schedule_failures, 'lambda a, b: clocked(a) and clocked(b)'), docs/testing.md says 'so no pair mixes two clocks', and decision tests-isolated-unless-declared rejects 'Take every start as a line's arrival less its seconds: a runner that writes its lines late, or a few milliseconds of noise, fails a round in which every test passed'; coding rule 3.6 bars elapsed time from two clocks. Trigger: a runner whose lines reach the stream a few milliseconds behind the worker, or whose seconds include setup begun before the earlier line arrived. Harm (A9): the preflight closes blocked naming a runner fault that does not exist, is refiled once, then stage_preflight raises a genuine blocker; in /ok-setup the owner is told to change a suite command that writes its lines correctly. Scope: caused; the check is new in this sprint. Report: i25.
note: Line-timing check now uses one clock per pair, as scripts/tests::schedule_failures and docs/testing.md do: where both lines carry started and ended, it compares the later started with the earlier ended on the suite command's clock; otherwise it compares the later arrived less seconds with the earlier arrived. The arrival comparison no longer applies to a clocked pair, so a runner whose lines arrive late no longer fails it. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md (check 5), plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md (3.7 check 1)

body: test-preflight.md checks 6 and 7, a scenario list with no recorded test: readings are (a) skip checks 6 and 7 whole, as ok-setup 3.7 ends its step, or (b) still check that the setup runs exit 0 and the scratch resource stands, and drop only the readiness test. Built (b): the setup's exit and the resource it must leave are checkable without a test.
checks/vendored-layer fails: pinned vendored path .ok-planner/lean-profiles.json is missing from the repo, so checks/run exits 1 (A9: the project's checks report failure).

Harm (A3, on the change): checks 6 and 7 cannot pass, the prompt says 'Where a check of the suite run, 5 to 7, fails, close blocked' (64-66), the write stage refiles once, and stage_preflight raises 'closed blocked twice ... surface it as a genuine blocker' (4503-4505), so the sprint's test stages stop on a check nothing can pass. The report's ok-setup half does not hold: skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md 3.7 line 127 says 'Where the scenario list records no test, say so in one line, and end the step', before its three checks. Scope: caused; checks 5 to 7 are new in this sprint. Report: i24.
- i41: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md:Check 5, and the same check in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md 3.7 check 1 (line 135). What it does: the line-timing check passes only where 'the later test's arrived less its seconds is at or after the earlier test's arrived, and, where both lines carry started and ended, the later test's started is at or after the earlier test's ended' (test-preflight.md:42-45): it applies the arrival test always, even where both lines carry the command's clock. arrived is the tests tool's monotonic clock (scripts/tests::take_line:2762, 'arrived = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)'); seconds is the suite command's. The schedule check takes the arrival span only where a pair is not clocked on the command's clock (scripts/tests::schedule_failures, 'lambda a, b: clocked(a) and clocked(b)'), docs/testing.md says 'so no pair mixes two clocks', and decision tests-isolated-unless-declared rejects 'Take every start as a line's arrival less its seconds: a runner that writes its lines late, or a few milliseconds of noise, fails a round in which every test passed'; coding rule 3.6 bars elapsed time from two clocks. Trigger: a runner whose lines reach the stream a few milliseconds behind the worker, or whose seconds include setup begun before the earlier line arrived. Harm (A9): the preflight closes blocked naming a runner fault that does not exist, is refiled once, then stage_preflight raises a genuine blocker; in /ok-setup the owner is told to change a suite command that writes its lines correctly. Scope: caused; the check is new in this sprint. Report: i25.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:ancestor_memory_lines. What it does: it decides whether claudeMdExcludes excludes an ancestor CLAUDE.md with 'not any(p == path or fnmatch.fnmatch(path, p) for p in patterns)' (true-up:959); fnmatch's * and ? match /, where the harness matches claudeMdExcludes as globs whose * stops at a path separator. Trigger: claudeMdExcludes ['/Users/*/CLAUDE.md'] and a project at /Users/me/work/proj with /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md: fnmatch counts the file excluded, diagnose prints no recommend line for it, and the harness still loads it into every session and agent. Harm (A8, a commitment of decision ancestor-claude-md-left-to-the-owner: 'The front door's administration names each such file that the project's harness settings do not already exclude'): the named report is skipped for a file the settings do not exclude. Scope: caused; ancestor_memory_lines is new in this sprint. Report: i38.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up: added path_glob(pattern), which compiles a claudeMdExcludes glob to a regex where * and ? stop at /, ** crosses folders, **/ matches zero or more folders, and [..] / [!..] classes never match /; ancestor_memory_lines now counts a file excluded only where an entry equals the path or its path_glob matches the whole path, replacing fnmatch.fnmatch, whose * crossed / and hid the recommend line for files the harness still loads. Dropped the now-unused fnmatch import (its only use). Enumeration: fnmatch had one site (true-up:959) plus the import at line 87. Checked: the cases /Users/*/CLAUDE.md vs /Users/me/work/CLAUDE.md (not excluded) and vs /Users/me/CLAUDE.md (excluded), ** and class cases; diagnose in a scratch nested project with claudeMdExcludes [<scratch>/*/CLAUDE.md] now prints the recommend line for <scratch>/a/b/CLAUDE.md. body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:step. What it does: step counts every open issued task ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]', scripts/tasks:867) into the run line's count, while next_claim takes only a task that is also ready ('... and ready(run, t)', 1121) and cmd_claim refuses one that still waits ('task %s still waits on %s; claim it once each of them closes', 1149). Boundary user no ruling names (R5, B213/B218, stored state): a run log the base release wrote, resumed by a new /goal or drained across an update. At the base a waiter issued before its dependency was refiled stayed issued, so such a log holds an open, issued task whose after names an open refile; tasks retry --all unissues it only where it reissues that refile, so a refile that stood open and unclaimed at the stop leaves the waiter issued. B213 says only 'the run log keeps its record shape'. Harm: next reports a count of claimable tasks no claim can take; the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md) starts an agent whose 'claim --agent' fails, refills on every return while another agent holds the refile, or returns stuck naming 'tasks retry' on a task left running, which does not apply. Scope: caused; the change made claim stricter than the issued mark step counts. Report: i30.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks::step now counts only issued tasks that are also ready: 'waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued") and ready(run, t)]', the same readiness next_claim requires and cmd_claim enforces, so the run line's count= never names a task no claim may take; an issued task with an open wait (a base-release run log's waiter of an open refile) now falls into the 'waiting running=N blocked=N' line until its waits close, and counts again then with no second issue. USAGE (module text and the 'tasks next' entry) says the count is of issued tasks whose waits have all closed. Driven in a scratch run: a waiter re-marked issued while its refile stood open printed 'count=1' for the refile alone, then 'waiting running=1 blocked=1' while the refile ran, and was claimed once the refile closed done. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:step. I201 makes next_claim skip, and cmd_claim refuse, an issued task whose after names a task not closed, but step counts every issued drainable task with no readiness check ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]'), so instructions prints it in the run line's count=. Trigger: a run log written by the base release holding an issued, unclaimed waiter of an open refile, resumed under decision stopped-run-resumes after /ok. Path: tasks next -> step -> instructions (count includes the waiter) -> the drain starts an agent -> tasks claim --agent -> next_claim skips it -> 'no issued task waits for profile ...' -> next prints the same count -> the drain starts another agent while the refile's agent runs, or returns stuck naming only 'tasks retry <task> on a task left running'. Harm (A9): the run line reports tasks waiting for an agent that no agent may claim, and the drain acts on it. Scope: caused; I201 added the claim-side check without the count-side one. Same flaw as i46 (sprint-10). Report: i21.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:open_waits (read by ready, step, next_claim, cmd_claim). Work item 'Refile holds its waiters until the refile closes' promises 'tasks claim never hands out a waiter before the refile closes'. open_waits counts a dependency satisfied when it is CLOSED whatever its outcome ('if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED'). Entry: tasks close <src> --outcome partial|blocked -> cmd_close -> step issues every drainable task where ready(run, t) -> the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md, filling every free slot) starts an agent -> next_claim/cmd_claim hand out the waiter. The session refiles only after that return (sprint-document step 7), when the waiter already runs; cmd_refile touches only waiters with state == OPEN, so it takes nothing back and the waiter builds on the unfinished stage. Evidence from this sprint's run (.ok-planner/sprints/2026-11-11-eighth-intake-drain-run.jsonl): t5 closed partial 07:17:06, waiter t6 claimed 07:17:17, refile t30 claimed 07:50:00; t11 closed partial 08:04:12, waiter t12 claimed 08:04:23; t28 closed partial 09:18:28, waiter t29 claimed 09:18:35, refile t34 claimed 09:20:46. Outcome reached only in part. Scope: the readiness rule stood at base; the work item's promised outcome fails through it. Report: i20.

fields.choice: readiness on any closed outcome is what the release's fix chains and drive relays rely on; changing it needs an owner ruling

note: open_waits counting a closed dependency as satisfied whatever its outcome stood at base, and users in the release rely on it: scripts/review's fix filing (the chunk loop near line 997) chains each duplicate group's chunks with --after the previous chunk, and a fixer that closes partial ('outside files:') is regrouped in the next round, never refiled, so its waiter must still run; skills/_converge/drive.md step 5 chains one-at-a-time drivers with --after, and a driver that records a broken stack closes blocked and is not refiled, so the next driver must still run. A done-only rule, or a rule that holds waiters until the closed task is refiled, stalls both chains forever. A rule scoped to some roles or declared per run would need sprint execution (plan-sprint/sprint-document.md, a sprint boilerplate the sprint-boilerplate check pins) to declare it: a new mechanism outside this file and beyond the work item, which names cmd_refile and the verbs that issue a task, and promises only that a waiter goes unclaimed while a refile stands open (at each claim the defect cites, no refile had been filed yet). It also changes, with no ruling, what a resumed base-release run log observes (stored state). Recorded as a question for the owner.

body: scripts/tasks::open_waits (read by ready, step, next_claim, cmd_claim): a wait is satisfied once its task closes, whatever the outcome, so a build stage closing partial or blocked frees its waiters before the session refiles it (this sprint's run: t5->t6, t11->t12, t28->t29). Readings: (a) satisfy a wait only on done, or on a closed task already refiled, and give converge's fix chains (scripts/review) and drive relays (skills/_converge/drive.md step 5) a release, since they never refile a partial fixer or a blocked driver; (b) a run config list of roles whose short close holds waiters until a refile, set by sprint execution in sprint-document.md beside swept_roles; (c) leave the tracker as it is and have sprint execution refile, or hold the drain, before the next claim. Built none: each changes users in the release or a sprint boilerplate, and resumed base-release run logs; i62 declined.
