body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:certification_failures judges contract item 3 from the defects pool and the review, sprint-pass, and drive tasks alone; it never reads the failures or reports pools, the merge tasks, or the owner-list task. Trigger: a certification ledger whose drive recorded a failure on the sprint's own story while its merge task stands open, or no merge was filed, and no owner list ran. Harm (A9): review certified prints 'SPRINT COMPLETE' and writes the -certified.txt mark over a find loop that did not finish: the failure was never merged into a defect nor filed in the intake, so 'done' depends on the session, against story certify-completion ('so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint') and the contract's item 3 (sprint-document.md:560-562, 'the run's find loop ran once, and every defect stands verified, declined, duplicate, stuck, or promised'), and converge SKILL.md:12 ('a merge agent folds every report into one defect list') and :61 ('Every report and failure the brief names that still stands open goes to the owner list'). Evidence: scripts/review:2073 'defects = json.loads(tasks_run(root, "--file", ledger, "item", "list", "--pool", "defects", ...))' is the only pool read; the driver reproduced exit 0 and SPRINT COMPLETE in a scratch project with merge t6 open and failure i1 open. In scope: the sprint's work item 'certified counts unrun drives' changed this function (it now refuses filed-but-unrun drivers and a review with no pass task) and the sprint moved the drive's merge into certification's step 5. From failures i10, i11.
note: scripts/review: certification_failures now adds find_loop_failures(root, ledger, tasks), which fails item 3 for each merge task of the ledger not closed, and, where no owner-list task closed done, for each reports or failures item standing open, backlog, judgment, or upstream (new constants OWNER_LIST_PROMPT, OWNER_LISTED_POOLS, OWNER_LISTED_STATES). So a drive failure no merge judged and no owner list filed keeps SPRINT NOT COMPLETE. .ok-planner/review/project.md: the certified description names the two new item 3 failures. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review, .ok-planner/review/project.md.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (pending loop) with planned_refile and mapped_waits. What it does: the pending loop walks blocked test tasks in key-string order (blocked_on_test_support sorts latest by key), gives each closed-blocked refile 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}' (holders[F] is the refile planned just before it, since planned_refile sets holders[F] to the new filing), and mapped_waits maps each copied wait to the planned refile of the task waited on ('filing["after"] = sorted({planned.get(dep, dep) for dep in latest})'). Trigger: two or more test tasks that share a test file and wait on each other through it close blocked having filed test-support items, where the waiting task's key sorts first as a string; with testing.chunk 1 and ten or more chunks of one story (test:S:1, test:S:10, ..., test:S:2), test:S:2's refile waits on test:S:12's through holders while test:S:10's refile waits on test:S:9's through its copied wait, which chains back through test:S:2, so the refiles wait on each other. The tracker's ready() (scripts/tasks:807-817) counts a dependency closed blocked as closed, so every chunk runs and can close blocked on one missing helper. Outcome not reached (C1, work item 'The write stage refiles a blocked test task that waits on another blocked test task', B24, with 'A test task takes a story's scenarios, up to testing.chunk'): loop_refusals refuses 'would wait on itself through ...', the write stage files nothing, and sprint-document step 7 makes that a genuine blocker. Scope: caused; at the base mapped_waits dropped a wait on a refile planned later, and chunk keys are new. Report: i26.
note: scripts/tests: stage_write's pending loop now walks blocked test tasks through refile_order(pending, successors), which orders them by their own after lists (mapped through latest_of to the pending set), ties in task order, instead of key-string order. A holders-derived wait then always points at the refile of a task the copied waits already put first, so the copied and holder waits agree and loop_refusals finds no cycle. Simulated with chunks test:S:1..12 sharing one file, each waiting on the one before: the old order gave 11 'would wait on itself' refusals, the new order none; a refile chain case (t11 refiled as t50, t12 after t11) also files with no refusal. File: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_verify. What it does: B22 (rewrite) groups every tests item awaiting its verifier by its recording task and keys the verify task 'verify:%s' % recorder, skipping a key already in existing (scripts/tests:4736-4743: 'awaiting.setdefault(item.get("task") or item["id"], []).append(item)', 'if ("verify", key) in existing: continue'); at the base the key was verify:<tests item id>. User left behind: the stopped-run resume path (decision stopped-run-resumes; sprint-document step 3 'tasks retry --all', which reopens a blocked or partial task under its own id, and step 4's '--stage verify after each drain'). Trigger: test task T closes blocked or partial having recorded scenario A's tests item; the verify stage files verify:T for A; the run stops before T is refiled; the resume reopens T under the same id; T records B. Before: B's item got verify:<B's item id>. Now: B groups under T, verify:T is in existing, and no verify task is ever filed for B; awaits_verifier(B) stays true, so --stage speed --from state refuses on it and the run cannot proceed (R3: a rewrite left a user in the release behind). Scope: caused by B22. Report: i28.
note: scripts/tests: stage_verify now skips only the tests items a verify task's brief already names (verify_briefed reads each verify task's 'tests item <id>:' lines, and the item id of an earlier release's verify:<item id> key), and keys a new batch for a recorder whose verify:<test task> key is taken as verify:<test task>:<n> (verify_key). So a reopened test task's later item B gets its own verify task, and awaits_verifier(B) no longer strands --stage speed. VERIFY_KEY replaces the three restated 'verify:%s' literals. .ok-planner/review/project.md: --stage verify's key description updated. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests, .ok-planner/review/project.md.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:undriven_failure, reached from certification_failures. What it does: certification_failures computes 'reason = undriven_reason(root, tasks) if undriven and not driven else None' (scripts/review, certification_failures); undriven_reason ends 'return "no driver task was filed"' where drive-stack prints none, or stack with no failed stack-start exec task; undriven_failure then writes 'its latest driver task %s %s' and appends '; the drive did not run: %s' % reason whenever reason differs. Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> where the ledger holds driver tasks for the required stories and none closed done with a result (each closed partial, or was never claimed), on this project (drive-stack none). Harm (A9): each item 3 line reads '<ledger> drove no story <slug>: its latest driver task tN closed partial; the drive did not run: no driver task was filed; ...', telling the operator acting on SPRINT NOT COMPLETE, and the stop record built from it, that no driver was filed in the line that names one. Scope: caused; B118 narrowed driven_stories to drivers that closed done, and the new undriven_failure appends the fallback beside a filed driver; at the base the fallback ran only where no driver task existed. Report: i31.
note: scripts/review: undriven_reason now returns None where it finds no reason (it returned the fallback 'no driver task was filed'). undriven_failure already writes 'no driver task was filed' itself when no driver exists, and appends '; the drive did not run: <reason>' only for a real reason (unfilled or refused drive commands, a failed stack start). So a line naming a filed driver no longer says no driver was filed. File: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review.

Scope: caused; the sprint added the deferral and the decision sentence. Report: i23.

body: .ok-planner/review/project.md, the review tool's certified description (it fails item 3 where 'no certification ledger names the rounds, where settled exits 2, ...'): it does not yet say that certified also fails item 3 for each deferred product-slow verdict that no open intake issue names by its site, which the i64 fix added in scripts/review:suite_failures. The fact file is stale, so a driver reads an incomplete contract.

scripts/review:unfiled_deferred: which issues count as the deferred verdict having reached the intake. Reading A counts open issues only, which matches the owner list's 'an open issue on the same site' rule. Reading B also counts archived issues closed as promoted. I built A. A certified rerun after the next /plan-sprint promotes the issue but before this sprint is archived would then fail item 3.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:step. What it does: step counts every open issued task ('waiting_for_agent = [t for t in drainable if t.get("issued")]', scripts/tasks:867) into the run line's count, while next_claim takes only a task that is also ready ('... and ready(run, t)', 1121) and cmd_claim refuses one that still waits ('task %s still waits on %s; claim it once each of them closes', 1149). Boundary user no ruling names (R5, B213/B218, stored state): a run log the base release wrote, resumed by a new /goal or drained across an update. At the base a waiter issued before its dependency was refiled stayed issued, so such a log holds an open, issued task whose after names an open refile; tasks retry --all unissues it only where it reissues that refile, so a refile that stood open and unclaimed at the stop leaves the waiter issued. B213 says only 'the run log keeps its record shape'. Harm: next reports a count of claimable tasks no claim can take; the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md) starts an agent whose 'claim --agent' fails, refills on every return while another agent holds the refile, or returns stuck naming 'tasks retry' on a task left running, which does not apply. Scope: caused; the change made claim stricter than the issued mark step counts. Report: i30.
note: Walked the trigger: a base-release log's issued waiter of an open refile. step (scripts/tasks:867) now counts only issued drainable tasks that are ready(run, t), the same rule next_claim (1121) and cmd_claim (1147) apply, so no run/exec line counts a task no claim or exec may take; such a waiter falls into the 'waiting running=N blocked=N' line and counts again once its waits close, issued mark kept. Exec lines get the same guard. No caller parses next's output programmatically; drain.md already describes the count as tasks whose dependencies are closed. USAGE wording updated in module text and the next entry. Only the step line and USAGE changed; no new accept-list harm. node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline on the file exits 0; py_compile passes.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:open_waits (read by ready, step, next_claim, cmd_claim). Work item 'Refile holds its waiters until the refile closes' promises 'tasks claim never hands out a waiter before the refile closes'. open_waits counts a dependency satisfied when it is CLOSED whatever its outcome ('if d is None or d["state"] != CLOSED'). Entry: tasks close <src> --outcome partial|blocked -> cmd_close -> step issues every drainable task where ready(run, t) -> the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md, filling every free slot) starts an agent -> next_claim/cmd_claim hand out the waiter. The session refiles only after that return (sprint-document step 7), when the waiter already runs; cmd_refile touches only waiters with state == OPEN, so it takes nothing back and the waiter builds on the unfinished stage. Evidence from this sprint's run (.ok-planner/sprints/2026-11-11-eighth-intake-drain-run.jsonl): t5 closed partial 07:17:06, waiter t6 claimed 07:17:17, refile t30 claimed 07:50:00; t11 closed partial 08:04:12, waiter t12 claimed 08:04:23; t28 closed partial 09:18:28, waiter t29 claimed 09:18:35, refile t34 claimed 09:20:46. Outcome reached only in part. Scope: the readiness rule stood at base; the work item's promised outcome fails through it. Report: i20.

fields.choice: readiness on any closed outcome is what the release's fix chains and drive relays rely on; changing it needs an owner ruling

note: Fixer's reason: open_waits treating any closed outcome as satisfied stood at base, and scripts/review's fix filing chains duplicate-group chunks with --after the previous chunk while a partial fixer is regrouped, not refiled, and skills/_converge/drive.md step 5 chains one-at-a-time drivers with --after while a blocked driver is not refiled, so a done-only rule stalls both; the work item promises only that refile takes back the issued mark of waiters that stand issued and unclaimed, and the cited claims came before any refile. Checked: scripts/review chunk loop (~997) and drive.md step 5 read as cited; sprint work item 'Refile holds its waiters until the refile closes' scopes to issued-and-unclaimed waiters; question recorded as calls item i76. Decline holds.

The sibling comparison in offer_groups still compares raw paths: 'claimed = claimed_paths(state["scenarios"])' then 'if path not in claimed:' against review.test_paths(root, tree_files(root, folders)), and claimed_paths adds scenario['test']['path'] and test_support_of(scenario) unnormalized. Rule: plumbline-coding rule 8 (a defect is one instance of a class; fix every member in the same change), which decides the fix. Trigger: the scenario list records a live test as './tests/a_test.py'. Path: tests offers / tests groups -> offer_groups lists tests/a_test.py in a legacy group as a file no scenario claims -> the owner takes the folder -> cmd_groups puts it in the sort list -> the sort planner may sort it delete -> the legacy task deletes a live test (A2). Scope: the sprint fixed one member of the class (I2) and changed both offer_groups (runtime group removed) and claimed_paths (test_support_of), leaving this member. Report: i18.
note: t60: claimed_paths (scripts/tests:1007) now normpaths each scenario test path and test support path; offer_groups' legacy branch compares them against review.test_paths over tests' tree_files, which normpaths every listed path (tests:840), so a scenario recorded as './tests/a_test.py' is claimed and leaves the legacy offer. body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:settled_failures, with cmd_settled and scripts/review:suite_failures. Decision test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests, amended by this sprint (.ok-planner/design/decisions/test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests.md:98-102), commits that review certified refuses a sprint 'with a speed send-back that neither settled, returned to its last passing version, nor, as a product-slow verdict a passing whole-suite round left standing, went to the intake'. settled_failures returns the deferred verdicts apart and never fails on them; cmd_settled prints 'SETTLED ... product-slow verdicts are deferred to the intake' and exits 0; review suite_failures takes exit 0 as item 3 holding (scripts/review:2185 'if ran.returncode == 0: return "holds ..."'). Nothing reads the intake for an issue on each deferred verdict's site. Trigger: the latest whole-suite round passes, a product-slow verdict stands deferred, and the owner list closes without filing its design issue (skipped, closed partial, or the run stopped after 2a). Outcome: review certified prints SPRINT COMPLETE though the verdict never reached the intake. The notes' call ('It does not check that the intake took them, since the owner list files them after it') holds for converge step 2a, not for review certified, which runs after the close. Scope: caused; the sprint added the deferral and the decision sentence. Report: i23.
note: t60: suite_failures (scripts/review) now, on a zero exit from tests settled, calls unfiled_deferred, which reads the same deferred list through 'tests failures --sprint --json' (cmd_failures prints deferred from unsettled_failures, as settled_failures does) and the open intake through issues.select(root) (live records with title and problem). Item 3 fails per deferred verdict whose site (path and function split on '::', or the scenario where no site) no open issue's title or problem names; owner-list.md files each deferred verdict's issue with the problem naming the site as path::function, so a filed issue matches. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:certification_failures judges contract item 3 from the defects pool and the review, sprint-pass, and drive tasks alone; it never reads the failures or reports pools, the merge tasks, or the owner-list task. Trigger: a certification ledger whose drive recorded a failure on the sprint's own story while its merge task stands open, or no merge was filed, and no owner list ran. Harm (A9): review certified prints 'SPRINT COMPLETE' and writes the -certified.txt mark over a find loop that did not finish: the failure was never merged into a defect nor filed in the intake, so 'done' depends on the session, against story certify-completion ('so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint') and the contract's item 3 (sprint-document.md:560-562, 'the run's find loop ran once, and every defect stands verified, declined, duplicate, stuck, or promised'), and converge SKILL.md:12 ('a merge agent folds every report into one defect list') and :61 ('Every report and failure the brief names that still stands open goes to the owner list'). Evidence: scripts/review:2073 'defects = json.loads(tasks_run(root, "--file", ledger, "item", "list", "--pool", "defects", ...))' is the only pool read; the driver reproduced exit 0 and SPRINT COMPLETE in a scratch project with merge t6 open and failure i1 open. In scope: the sprint's work item 'certified counts unrun drives' changed this function (it now refuses filed-but-unrun drivers and a review with no pass task) and the sprint moved the drive's merge into certification's step 5. From failures i10, i11.
note: t59: scripts/review certification_failures now adds find_loop_failures: each role=merge task not closed fails item 3 (driver_standing names how it stands), and where no prompt=owner-list task closed done, each reports/failures item at open, backlog, judgment, or upstream fails it. Walked the trigger: merge open with failure open -> failure line; no merge and no owner list with failure open -> failure line; a run whose owner list closed done and every merge closed adds nothing. owner-list prompt name matches converge SKILL.md:134 and drive SKILL.md:35; an empty pool lists [] (checked). project.md certified sentence matches. Only caller is certification_failures. plumbline exits 0 on both files.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write (pending loop) with planned_refile and mapped_waits. What it does: the pending loop walks blocked test tasks in key-string order (blocked_on_test_support sorts latest by key), gives each closed-blocked refile 'waits |= {holders[path] for path in task.get("files") or [] if path in holders}' (holders[F] is the refile planned just before it, since planned_refile sets holders[F] to the new filing), and mapped_waits maps each copied wait to the planned refile of the task waited on ('filing["after"] = sorted({planned.get(dep, dep) for dep in latest})'). Trigger: two or more test tasks that share a test file and wait on each other through it close blocked having filed test-support items, where the waiting task's key sorts first as a string; with testing.chunk 1 and ten or more chunks of one story (test:S:1, test:S:10, ..., test:S:2), test:S:2's refile waits on test:S:12's through holders while test:S:10's refile waits on test:S:9's through its copied wait, which chains back through test:S:2, so the refiles wait on each other. The tracker's ready() (scripts/tasks:807-817) counts a dependency closed blocked as closed, so every chunk runs and can close blocked on one missing helper. Outcome not reached (C1, work item 'The write stage refiles a blocked test task that waits on another blocked test task', B24, with 'A test task takes a story's scenarios, up to testing.chunk'): loop_refusals refuses 'would wait on itself through ...', the write stage files nothing, and sprint-document step 7 makes that a genuine blocker. Scope: caused; at the base mapped_waits dropped a wait on a refile planned later, and chunk keys are new. Report: i26.
note: t59: scripts/tests stage_write's pending loop walks refile_order(pending, successors): task order, each task placed after the pending tasks its after list names (through latest_of), so a holders-derived wait always points at a refile the copied waits put first. Simulated with blocked_on_test_support, planned_refile, mapped_waits, and loop_refusals on chunks test:S:1..12 sharing one file, each after the one before: the old key-string order gives 11 'would wait on itself' refusals, refile_order gives none. The body of the loop is unchanged; plumbline exits 0.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_verify. What it does: B22 (rewrite) groups every tests item awaiting its verifier by its recording task and keys the verify task 'verify:%s' % recorder, skipping a key already in existing (scripts/tests:4736-4743: 'awaiting.setdefault(item.get("task") or item["id"], []).append(item)', 'if ("verify", key) in existing: continue'); at the base the key was verify:<tests item id>. User left behind: the stopped-run resume path (decision stopped-run-resumes; sprint-document step 3 'tasks retry --all', which reopens a blocked or partial task under its own id, and step 4's '--stage verify after each drain'). Trigger: test task T closes blocked or partial having recorded scenario A's tests item; the verify stage files verify:T for A; the run stops before T is refiled; the resume reopens T under the same id; T records B. Before: B's item got verify:<B's item id>. Now: B groups under T, verify:T is in existing, and no verify task is ever filed for B; awaits_verifier(B) stays true, so --stage speed --from state refuses on it and the run cannot proceed (R3: a rewrite left a user in the release behind). Scope: caused by B22. Report: i28.
note: t59: scripts/tests stage_verify skips only items verify_briefed finds: the 'tests item <id>: ' lines test_verify_line opens each brief line with (re.M), plus the item id an earlier release's verify:<item id> key names. A recorder whose verify:<task> key exists gets verify:<task>:<n> from verify_key, so the reopened T's later item B gets its own verify task and no longer strands --stage speed; A, already briefed, is not filed twice. Each test task records a new tests item, and verifiers only set an item's state away from open, so no item is reopened and then skipped. The fixes/promises keys keep verify:<item id> through VERIFY_KEY. project.md --stage verify sentence matches. plumbline exits 0.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:undriven_failure, reached from certification_failures. What it does: certification_failures computes 'reason = undriven_reason(root, tasks) if undriven and not driven else None' (scripts/review, certification_failures); undriven_reason ends 'return "no driver task was filed"' where drive-stack prints none, or stack with no failed stack-start exec task; undriven_failure then writes 'its latest driver task %s %s' and appends '; the drive did not run: %s' % reason whenever reason differs. Trigger: review certified --sprint <path> where the ledger holds driver tasks for the required stories and none closed done with a result (each closed partial, or was never claimed), on this project (drive-stack none). Harm (A9): each item 3 line reads '<ledger> drove no story <slug>: its latest driver task tN closed partial; the drive did not run: no driver task was filed; ...', telling the operator acting on SPRINT NOT COMPLETE, and the stop record built from it, that no driver was filed in the line that names one. Scope: caused; B118 narrowed driven_stories to drivers that closed done, and the new undriven_failure appends the fallback beside a filed driver; at the base the fallback ran only where no driver task existed. Report: i31.
note: t59: scripts/review undriven_reason returns None where it finds no reason; undriven_failure writes 'no driver task was filed' only where no driver exists and appends '; the drive did not run: <reason>' only for a real reason (unfilled, a refused drive command, a failed stack start). So with drive-stack none and drivers closed partial, the line names the latest driver and its standing alone. certification_failures is the only caller and passes the None through. plumbline exits 0.

body: Reviewed /converge (SKILL.md, prompts fix/verify/restore/merge/owner-list/hunt-*, _converge blocks, drain) and ran its mechanical path in a scratch project (backlog -> merges -> snapshot -> fixes -> verifies x2 -> stuck -> restores -> restores --verify -> owner list revise): all verbs worked. Divergence: fix.md line 73 tells a fixer 'A fix that must change a behavior a user across a boundary observes, where no ruling allows it, is declined with a question recorded: that change is the owner's to rule on.' But verify.md line 26 (Check each defect) defines the declines a verifier accepts exhaustively: 'A declined defect is not real, the accept list leaves it standing, or its fix lies only in a file the fix line rule above leaves alone' -- the boundary-question decline is not among them, so a verifier following the text sends it back (kickbacks+1) until the defect goes stuck at fix.max_kickbacks, its code restored, and it reaches the owner as a 'Stuck in <run>' issue, or the fixer is pushed to change the boundary behavior without the owner. owner-list.md ('A decline the fixer made with a question recorded ... turns its issue into a judgment issue', under defects 'declined ... with a verified field') and the cheatsheet's Defect issues section ('a verified decline that waits on a boundary question') both presume verifiers accept it. The story promises: defects found and fixed without the owner, so that the owner meets only the questions that need their judgment -- the boundary question should reach the owner as that question, after one decline, not after spent fix rounds as a stuck defect; decision converge-finds-then-fixes: 'A defect whose fixes a verifier rejected up to the limit is no longer mechanical' (stuck is for failed fixes, not for a decline the rules call for). Evidence: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/verify.md:26 vs plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/fix.md:73 and owner-list.md:102.
note: verify-refuses-boundary-question-declines

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 3 (Reconcile), section 9 step 1, section 14 step 4, and {{PLANNING-HANDOFF}} in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md, against the sprint document's execution step 2 and decision:closing-commit-baseline. The Reconcile window covers only what stands at Reconcile time: SKILL.md says 'Compute the window. git log --oneline <closed>..HEAD plus the uncommitted tree.' Out-of-band work that appears later in the same session (a path edited during the dialogue, drafting, or code planning) is never sent to the out-of-band reviewer. Code planning step 1 only names such paths ('Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name it to the owner in one line; the planner reads the working tree as it stands'), and the handoff then commits them before the base: '{{PLANNING-HANDOFF}}: Where it lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name every such path to the owner, grouped by the work each belongs to, such as ... "out-of-band code" ... ask the owner once whether to commit them'. Those commits land before execution writes its -base.txt, so sprint certification (which judges base..tree) never reviews them, and they land before this sprint's closed: stamp, so the next /plan-sprint's window (closed..HEAD) never contains them either. The same holds for any commit made between approval and the execution base step, which refuses only uncommitted paths ('Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, stop'). No text compares the handoff's paths with what Reconcile reviewed. The story promises: 'an interactive ceremony that turns my goals - and the open design questions and unreconciled work that bear on them - into a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint'. Saw: out-of-band work committed by the handoff, or between approval and the base, falls between two windows and is reconciled by no session, so the corpus can silently disagree with code no ceremony ever reviewed. Fix direction for the owner: rerun the out-of-band review over paths that changed after Reconcile before the handoff commits them, or have the handoff refuse to commit paths Reconcile did not see.
note: plan-sprint-skips-out-of-band-work-after-reconcile

body: Reviewed the How to execute this sprint boilerplate (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md), the drain loop it names (skills/_tasks/drain.md), and the tracker verbs they call (next, close, report, render, run against a scratch project). Step 4, in a sprint that opens test stages, tells the session to drain inside step 4 itself, before the step that creates the checklist: line 287, 'Drain with step 7's loop. After each drain, run tests tasks --sprint <this sprint's path> --stage verify ...'. The test write stage is filed --after the code stages' build tasks, so that drain runs every build stage. The checklist step comes later in reading order, step 6 at line 327-329: 'Keep the progress checklist. ... Create one entry per stage when the build tasks are filed.' A session working the numbered steps in order, under testing on (as this project runs), lands every code stage in step 4's drain before it reaches step 6, so the owner's session shows no checklist while the stages land. The story promises: 'a way to see from my session which stages of a running sprint have landed, each time the run reports back to my session'. Decision task-tools-mirror-the-report: 'The checklist is its own numbered step, with its three moments named, because an executor skips a checklist written as a trailing clause after the report-rendering step: a measured execution under that form ran its first three agents with no checklist'. Step 6 names its moment by event, but step 4's embedded drain puts the first drain ahead of it in the order the executor reads, the same failure the decision names. The rest holds: true-up diagnose prints 'WIRING NEEDED (ok-planner, env)' with the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS entry, wire-env writes it and repairs a value of 0, and the Workflow return's step 3 reads keys from tasks report's key column, which the tracker prints.
note: test-stage-drain-precedes-progress-checklist
